problems.title: Probability of a set difference
problems.question: P(A)=0.7, P(B)=0.6, P(A∪B)=0.9. FindP(A\B).
problems.idea: Use an exact probability, sequence or coordinate relation and verify its conditions.
steps: The union consists of B plus the part of A outside B. Thus the answer is 0.9−0.6=0.3.

problems.title: Mean and median of equally spaced data
problems.question: Ten consecutive odd numbers have mean8 greater than their range. Find the median.
problems.idea: Use an exact probability, sequence or coordinate relation and verify its conditions.
formulas: The range is 9·2=18. For an arithmetic list, the mean and median both equal the midpoint of its endpoints.
steps: The mean is 18+8=26, so the median is 26.

problems.title: A geometric term above ten
problems.question: Forb_n=2^n/128, find the leastn withb_n>10.
problems.idea: Use an exact probability, sequence or coordinate relation and verify its conditions.
steps: 2¹⁰=1024 is too small, while2¹¹=2048 exceeds1280. Thusn=11.

problems.title: Collinear coordinate vectors
problems.question: A=(−1,2), B=(0,−2), C=(3,3), D=(4,−2). Which listed vector is collinear with(−0.2,1)?
problems.idea: Use an exact probability, sequence or coordinate relation and verify its conditions.
steps: It is a nonzero scalar multiple, so CD is collinear with the given vector.

problems.title: Centroid vector from two side vectors
problems.question: O is the centroid of ABC, BC=a, AC=b as vectors. ExpressBO.
problems.idea: Use an exact probability, sequence or coordinate relation and verify its conditions.
steps: BA=BC−AC=a−b. HenceBO=(2a−b)/3.

problems.title: Uniform area probability in an annulus
problems.question: Two concentric circles have radii5,4. A point is uniform in the larger disk. Find probability it lies outside the smaller disk.
problems.idea: Use an exact probability, sequence or coordinate relation and verify its conditions.
steps: The ratio is(25π−16π)/(25π)=9/25.

problems.title: A pie-chart angle represents seven students
problems.question: The sector for grade8 exceeds grade9 by 15°. Seven more students receive8 than 9. Find total students.
problems.idea: Use an exact probability, sequence or coordinate relation and verify its conditions.
formulas: An angle difference 15° is 15/360=1/24 of the whole count.
steps: Thus7=N/24, so N=168.

problems.title: Internal division of a coordinate segment
problems.question: A=(−2,7), B=(2,−1), AK:KB=1:3. Find the coordinate sum of K.
problems.idea: Use an exact probability, sequence or coordinate relation and verify its conditions.
steps: B−A=(4,−8), so K=(−1,5). The coordinate sum is 4.

problems.title: Distance between parallel lines
problems.question: Lines y=2√2x+3 and y=2√2x+b are distance 2 apart. Find the product of possibleb.
problems.idea: Use an exact probability, sequence or coordinate relation and verify its conditions.
steps: Set|b−3|=6. The values are 9 and −3, whose product is −27.

problems.title: Middle term of seven arithmetic terms
problems.question: In an arithmetic progression, S₁₁−S₄=210. Finda₈.
problems.idea: Use an exact probability, sequence or coordinate relation and verify its conditions.
formulas: The difference isa₅+…+a₁₁, seven terms with middle terma₈.
steps: Their sum is 7a₈, so a₈=210/7=30.

problems.title: Two independent draws with replacement
problems.question: Draw twice from cards1,…,9, with replacement. What is the probability the first number is larger?
problems.idea: Use an exact probability, sequence or coordinate relation and verify its conditions.
formulas: There are 81 ordered pairs;9 are ties. The remaining72 split equally by symmetry.
steps: Thus36 pairs have the first larger, for probability 36/81=4/9.

problems.title: At least one independent success
problems.question: Independent pass probabilities are 0.8 and 0.75. Find the probability of passing at least one.
problems.idea: Use an exact probability, sequence or coordinate relation and verify its conditions.
formulas: The complementary event is failing both.
steps: Its probability is 0.2·0.25=0.05. Thus at least one pass has probability 1−0.05=0.95.

problems.title: Incenter of a coordinate isosceles triangle
problems.question: A=(−2,2), B=(4,10), C=(10,2). Find the coordinate sum of the incenter.
problems.idea: Use an exact probability, sequence or coordinate relation and verify its conditions.
formulas: The equal sides have length 10, the base12, are a 48, andsemiperimeter16. Thusr=48/16=3.
steps: The symmetry axis is x=4. Since the base is y=2, the incenter lies at y=2+r=5.
Its coordinates are(4,5), with sum 9.

problems.title: Use a dot product after forming the vector
problems.question: a=(2,−1), b=(1,3), c=(−1,5). Find the angle between|a|²b+|b|²a and c.
problems.idea: Use an exact probability, sequence or coordinate relation and verify its conditions.
steps: The constructed vector is 5(1,3)+10(2,−1)=(25,5). Its dot product with c is −25+25=0.
Both vectors are nonzero, so their angle is 90°.

problems.title: Reordered arithmetic terms in a geometric progression
problems.question: Distinct second, fourth, third terms of an arithmetic progression for m a geometric progression in that order. Find its ratio.
problems.idea: Use an exact probability, sequence or coordinate relation and verify its conditions.
formulas: Let those terms bet, t+2d, t+d, with d≠0. Then(t+2d)²=t(t+d).
steps: Expansion givesd(3t+4d)=0, so t=−4d/3.
The geometric ratio is(t+2d)/t=(2d/3)/(−4d/3)=−1/2.

problems.title: Use the complementary square
problems.question: A uniform point(x, y) lies in the unit square. FindP(min(x, y)≤0.4).
problems.idea: Use an exact probability, sequence or coordinate relation and verify its conditions.
formulas: The complement has bothx>0.4 and y>0.4.
steps: That square has side 0.6 andarea0.36. The requested probability is 1−0.36=0.64.

problems.title: Keep a dot product strictly negative
problems.question: For every realx, the angle between(−x, p) and(x−1,1) must be obtuse or straight. Findp.
problems.idea: Use an exact probability, sequence or coordinate relation and verify its conditions.
steps: It must be strictly negative for allx, including the maximiserx=1/2. Thusp+1/4<0.
Conversely, p<−1/4 ensures a negative dot product and nonzero vectors for allx.

problems.title: Order alternating-sign geometric terms
problems.question: Nine geometric terms satisfyb₃<b₅<b₄. Which term is the median?
problems.idea: Use an exact probability, sequence or coordinate relation and verify its conditions.
steps: These inequalities force r∈(−1,0) andb₃<0. Thus all five odd-index terms are negative and increase:b₁<b₃<b₅<b₇<b₉.
The four even-index terms are positive. Therefore the fifth value in increasing order, the median, isb₉.

problems.title: Two slopes make a forty-five-degree angle
problems.question: Find the sum of allafor which2x+3y+199=0 and ax−y+9=0 make a 45° line angle.
problems.idea: Use an exact probability, sequence or coordinate relation and verify its conditions.
steps: Solve3a+2=±(3−2a). The values are a=1/5 and −5.
Their sum is −24/5=−4.8.

problems.title: An infinite geometric subsequence
problems.question: Choose terms from 1/3,1/9,1/27,… to for m an infinite geometric progression. Which listed total is possible?
problems.idea: Use an exact probability, sequence or coordinate relation and verify its conditions.
formulas: Choose first term 1/9 andratio1/9, giving terms with exponents2,4,6,… .
steps: The sum is(1/9)/(1−1/9)=1/8, one of the choices.

problems.title: Symmetric roots that form an arithmetic progression
problems.question: For how many integerado the distinct real roots ofx⁴−10x²+a=0 for m an arithmetic progression with at least3 terms?
problems.idea: Use an exact probability, sequence or coordinate relation and verify its conditions.
formulas: Three roots must be−r,0, r, forcing a=0. Four roots must be−3t,−t, t,3t.
steps: For four roots, the squared positive roots sum tot²+9t²=10, so t²=1 and their product is a=9.
Botha=0 and 9 work. The case of only two distinct roots is excluded. Thus there are 2 integer parameters.

problems.title: Farthest circle point from a line
problems.question: Find the maximum distance from a point onx²+y²=2x−6y+15 to 3x−4y+10=0.
problems.idea: Use an exact probability, sequence or coordinate relation and verify its conditions.
formulas: The circle is(x−1)²+(y+3)²=25, with centre(1,−3), radius 5.
steps: The centre-to-line distance is|3+12+10|/5=5. The farthest circle distance is 5+5=10.

problems.title: Median and altitude directions from side vectors
problems.question: AB=(2,−6), AC=(−2,−2). Find the smaller angle between the A-median and A-altitude.
problems.idea: Use an exact probability, sequence or coordinate relation and verify its conditions.
formulas: The median vector is(AB+AC)/2=(0,−4). The base direction is BC=AC−AB=(−4,4).
steps: The median is vertical. The altitude is perpendicular to slope−1, so has slope1.
Its smaller angle with the vertical is 45°.
